rationale: No supported optimization is safely applicable to this workflow. The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache pattern has measured evidence, but this C/C++ autotools workflow installs system packages via apt-get/apk across a matrix of many different OS and container combinations (ubuntu:14.04 through ubuntu:26.04, alpine:3.18 through 3.22, plus direct runners on ubuntu-22.04/24.04). There is no language-specific dependency directory or lockfile to key a cache on, and caching /var/cache/apt/archives across heterogeneous container images and runner OS versions would not be a minimal, safe change; the pattern's precondition that cache inputs include lockfile and environment is not cleanly met. The P-LIT-FAIL-FAST pattern (set fail-fast: true on the build matrix) is not supported because the required_checks status is not_verified and the 14-configuration matrix appears to be a multi-platform compatibility matrix where every outcome is required, matching the contraindication that every matrix outcome is required and full failure diagnostics are needed. Other patterns (cancel stale runs, change filtering, timeouts, schedule suppression, test selection/prioritization) either operate at CI-service scope rather than workflow scope, have contraindications that apply (required checks must run on each revision, continuous monitoring may be mandatory, strict contract requires full test set), or lack verified preconditions for this repository. Preserving intended build and test coverage means no change is warranted.
